01 / FOUNDATIONS

Color roles

Usage and opacity

Use roughly 60% cream canvas, 30% white panels and content surfaces, and 10% teal actions, selection, and focus accents. The canvas is Amber 50 at 50% over white (resolved #FFFDF5). Headings stay near-black, body text stays dark gray, and chips, Sent, and destructive actions retain their functional colors. Choose colors by role and interaction state.

Typography

Choose by purpose

Inter

Navigation, controls, titles, and reading text.

Newsreader

The homepage greeting and the optional serif article format.

Use six shared text sizes: 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, and 30 px. Choose by purpose, with size, line height, and weight defined together. Responsive variants stay with their role; icons use a separate 16, 20, 24, and 40 px scale.

Role-based organization follows Material typography guidance and Carbon typography strategies. Samples use the app’s shared typography roles. Project grid-card headings use 16 px Semibold, dropdown values use 14 px Regular, and status badges match settings chips at 12 px Medium with a 20 px line height.

Spacing

Padding & gaps

Use shared spacing values for padding and gaps to keep controls and sections consistent.

The primary rhythm is 4 px. Smaller refinements are available in the token inventory.

4 shared shapes

Use the component’s assigned radius to keep corners consistent.

Surfaces

Subtle menu elevation
Dropdown
Popover
Dialog

Structural navigation/sidebar, New Draft, Content, editor, and source panels use white. The selected joined editor tab matches its panel; inner cards, fields, menus, and dialogs remain white. Dropdowns and popovers share a white surface, 1 px neutral border, 8 px corners, and a 0px 4px 12px shadow at 8% opacity on desktop and 16% on mobile. Mobile dialogs and open workspace panels share New Project’s 16% backdrop and 2px blur. Grid project cards and list rows gain a subtle 0px 3px 10px black shadow at 7% opacity on hover. Their hover surfaces remain white with dark text. List rows use 1 px inset teal top and bottom rules on hover or focus within, matching the grid-card hover color without side strokes or changes to row geometry. Keyboard-focus outlines remain visible.

Iconography

CSA icon library

Unselected: outlined (FILL 0). Selected: filled (FILL 1). Apply this rule to icons in selection controls, including view switches, source folders, and formatting toggles. Actions without a selected state use filled icons.

The gallery includes current and legacy app icons. Continue and Upload appear in New Project, and Search marks article URL entry. Document and Source Link remain available from older flows. The legacy result-thumbnail photo_camera glyph remains app-only and is excluded from this gallery. Each icon shows both states and its Material Symbols name. Glyph sizes use a separate 16, 20, 24, and 40 px scale. The default is 24 px; status badge icons use 16 px.

02 / COMPONENTS

The pieces of the workspace.

These specimens reuse the app’s production classes, tokens, and shared helpers. Try the controls with isolated example data.

Primary uses white text on Teal 700 (#00786F), Teal 800 (#005F5A) on hover or press, and Neutral 200 (#E5E5E5) with Neutral 500 (#737373) text when disabled. Secondary (Cancel) keeps a white surface with teal text and outline, darker teal on hover, and neutral disabled colors. Tertiary uses teal text without a resting border; hover or press uses a #E5E5E5 fill with a darker teal label and no visible border. Destructive (Delete) retains its red default and hover colors. The middle column previews hover. Keyboard focus uses a visible Teal 700 ring.

Text contrast: white on Teal 700 measures 5.36:1; white on Teal 800 measures 7.54:1. Teal 700 text on the cream canvas measures 5.27:1, and on the soft Teal 50 selected surface measures 5.14:1. Enabled and hover action labels meet the 4.5:1 normal-text AA target. Disabled states are exempt from contrast minimums.

Draft status tabs

Your draft requests will appear here.

Content to Draft and Drafted use text tabs with a light-gray baseline and a teal underline beneath the selected teal label. Labels use Inter Medium (500), with a 16 px gap. Switching updates the content immediately, then fades the new panel in over 200 ms with ease timing. Label and underline colors use the same transition. Arrow keys, Home, and End select and focus a tab; Tab reaches the selected tab. Reduced motion switches immediately.

Status labels match settings chips: Inter Medium (500), 12 px with a 20 px line height. Status badges keep shared detail corners (4 px), and settings chips keep pill corners. Format uses Rose 200, Audience uses Indigo 100, and Voice uses Orange 200; drafting shimmer steps share these category colors. Pair status color with its label and icon.

Selection fields

14 px / 400 · 36 px desktop · 46 px mobile

Empty dropdowns show their purpose—Format, Audience, or Voice—in Inter Regular (400) on a white surface. Choosing a value displays the selection. Selected recipe and WordPress destination options keep neutral text and row backgrounds, with a teal checkmark showing selection. Pointer hover stays gray and keyboard focus keeps its visible outline. Choosing None Selected from the menu clears the value and restores the purpose label.

Text-field and checkbox boundaries

Neutral 500 · 3:1 minimum

Text fields and unchecked checkboxes use Neutral 500 through component.field.border and component.checkbox.border. Contrast measures 4.74:1 on white, 4.66:1 on the Amber 50 at 50% over white (#FFFDF5) page canvas, and 4.35:1 on Neutral 100, above the 3:1 requirement for control boundaries.

Neutral 200 remains for decorative card, panel, and divider borders, plus dropdown outlines identified by dark labels and chevrons. Selected checkboxes use Teal 700 (#00786F) fills with white checks. Selected borders and keyboard-focus outlines use the same teal accent.

Toast notifications

5.5 seconds · 9 seconds with Undo
Source deleted

A white toast with dark message text, a subtle border and shadow, and an optional icon-only Undo action. The filled Material Symbols undo icon has an accessible Undo label and a pointer tooltip. Standard messages dismiss after 5.5 seconds; messages with Undo dismiss after 9 seconds. Undo shows Source restored for 5.5 seconds. Show Toast Again previews the timed notification.

Content card

Drafted

Standard FormatGeneral AudienceUS Weekly

Pending is content added to To Draft before a draft has been created. It starts selected, with a teal dashed border, its generated heading, and Format, Audience, and Voice chips. Pending and drafted content cards have no word-count pill or source counter. Select or deselect the card with its main button; the pressed state exposes selection to assistive technology. Draft is enabled only while selected. Draft previews the ready card. Default and Selected preview the drafted card’s inactive and active states. Settings stay on one line with an overflow fade. The pencil opens the same red Delete menu in every state; Restore Sample returns a deleted specimen. These controls change only this reference.

Project cards & list rows

Homepage components

The app’s project title, update date, content count, layout switch, and action menu use isolated example data here.

Project dates, content counts, and enabled ellipsis icons on white use Neutral 500 (#737373) at 4.74:1. Supporting text directly on the resolved canvas (#FFFDF5) uses semantic.color.text.canvas-secondary (#404040) at 10.18:1. Neutral 500 is 4.66:1 on the resolved canvas, meeting both the 4.5:1 normal-text and 3:1 essential-icon minimums. Essential icons and state indicators need 3:1. The selected layout uses Teal 700 (#00786F) with a white icon, providing 5.36:1 contrast. Decorative card and divider borders may remain Neutral 200 when readable labels or icons identify the controls; keyboard focus must remain visible.

04 / HANDOFF

Ready to use and maintain.

The app now reads its shared values from the same token source as this reference.

Use the system

  1. Edit dist/design-system/tokens.json.
  2. Run npm run design-system:build.
  3. Use a semantic or component CSS variable.
  4. Run npm run check and review desktop and mobile.
.primary-action {
  background: var(--csa-component-button-primary-background);
  color: var(--csa-component-button-primary-label);
  height: var(--csa-component-button-height);
  border-radius: var(--csa-component-button-radius);
}

Keep generated CSS, flat JSON, and CSV in sync. The check command detects stale exports, unresolved references, cycles, and CSS naming collisions.

Design-tool handoff

Use DTCG-compatible JSON in a token importer that supports the 2025.10 format. CSV includes slash-separated design names, resolved values, aliases, and descriptions for manual mapping.

Map colors and dimensions to variables where supported. Map typography to text styles. Check alias and composite support in your importer.

Original extraction: CSA b92005e. This local reference now uses the approved cream, white, and teal palette, consolidated type scale, and shared component roles. Unused previous-theme colors have been removed from the token inventory.

Responsive behavior

≤ 768 px
Mobile navigation, stacked canvas, 46 px selection fields, 44 px touch targets.
≥ 769 px
Desktop navigation and workspace panels.
≤ 1100 px
Editor layout adapts before the mobile navigation breakpoint.
999 / 579 px
Dashboard container widths switch to two and one columns.

Additional component-specific breakpoints: 700, 650, 480, and 370 px. Write source media and container query thresholds with token(foundation.breakpoint.name). The design-system build resolves these to literal values in generated CSS because custom properties cannot replace query thresholds.

Motion & review notes

Most interactions run 120–200 ms. The homepage greeting, grid cards, and list rows fade in and glide upward 40 px together over 300 ms with ease-in-out timing, without a delay or stagger. Reduced motion shows the greeting, grid cards, and list rows immediately.

The approved palette uses cream canvas, white panels and inner surfaces, and teal interaction accents. Muted text on white is 2.52:1 and is reserved for inactive controls and decoration; white on primary teal is 5.36:1. Readable supporting text and enabled menu icons use Secondary on white; supporting text directly on the resolved canvas uses canvas-secondary (#404040), with 10.18:1 contrast. Headings stay near-black and body text stays dark gray. Selected borders, active labels, and focus indicators use teal; selected supporting surfaces use Teal 50. Drafting cards stay white and keep the fixed dark label “Drafting Content”. Timed paper phases advance through the selected-category shimmer colors in Format/Audience/Voice order: pink, lavender, then peach, skipping unselected categories. One selected category keeps its color. Reduced motion hides the shimmer sweep and keeps a static paper and label.

The radius scale is standardized. Other observed values and component exceptions remain documented in the inventory.

References: DTCG Format 2025.10 · WCAG contrast minimum
